gloss: to get sunburned; to get a tan; to fade from sunlight

forms.label: Past polite
forms.negative: {日焼|ひや}けしませんでした

forms.label: ている past
forms.negative: {日焼|ひや}けしていなかった

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {日焼|ひや}けしていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to get sunburned; to get a tan; to become darkened by the sun
definitions.explanation: For skin to darken or burn from exposure to sunlight. Covers both deliberate tanning and accidental sunburn.

definitions.gloss: to fade from sunlight; to become discolored by sun exposure
definitions.explanation: For paper, fabric, photographs, or other materials to fade, yellow, or become damaged from prolonged exposure to sunlight.

examples.english: I got tanned in the summer.

examples.japanese: {海|うみ}で{日焼|ひや}けして{肌|はだ}が{赤|あか}くなった。
examples.english: I got sunburned at the beach and my skin turned red.

examples.japanese: {日焼|ひや}け{止|ど}めを{塗|ぬ}らないと{日焼|ひや}けしやすい。
examples.english: If you don't put on sunscreen, you'll burn easily.

examples.japanese: カーテンが{日焼|ひや}けして{色|いろ}が{褪|あ}せた。
examples.english: The curtains faded from sun exposure.

examples.japanese: {窓際|まどぎわ}に{置|お}いていたので、{写真|しゃしん}がすっかり{日焼|ひや}けしてしまった。
examples.english: Because I had left it by the window, the photograph became completely sun-faded.

notes:
A する-verb from the noun {日焼|ひや}け, composed of {日|ひ} (sun) + {焼|や}け (burning, from {焼|や}ける). The noun {日焼|ひや}け is used independently for sunburn/tan or sun damage.

USAGE:
For skin (sense 1), Japanese does not strongly distinguish between "tan" (gradual browning) and "sunburn" (painful reddening) — both are {日焼|ひや}け. Context clarifies. The compound {日焼|ひや}け{止|ど}め (sunscreen) is one of the most common related words.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {日焼|ひや}け{止|ど}め — sunscreen
- {日焼|ひや}けサロン — tanning salon
- {日焼|ひや}け{跡|あと} — tan lines; sun marks
- {日焼|ひや}けした{肌|はだ} — tanned/sunburned skin

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {焼|や}ける — to burn (broader; cooking, fire, jealousy)
- {色|いろ}{褪|あ}せる — to fade, to lose color (general fading, not only from sun)
- {変色|へんしょく}する — to discolor, to change color (technical; any color change)
